source.title: Language Surgery in Multilingual Large Language Models
source.authors: Joanito Agili Lopo; Muhammad Ravi Shulthan Habibi; Tack Hwa Wong; Muhammad Ilham Ghozali; Fajri Koto; Genta Indra Winata; Peerat Limkonchotiwat; Alham Fikri Aji; Samuel Cahyawijaya

page_placements.theme: Within-model cross-language alignment depends on depth, resources and content

record.tranche_reason: Extends representation-alignment analysis to multilingual LLMs, measuring cross-language alignment within models across layers; it does not test the specified cross-model convergence versions.
record.gate_note: The study measures cosine similarity for parallel sentences across languages within each model, not similarity between independently trained models. Its LID and downstream-task results are related analyses, but do not measure any listed claim version. The alignment results are aggregated across seven datasets; no separate numerical outcomes for each dataset are stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The study measures within-model cross-language alignment (cosine similarity of parallel sentences across languages inside LaBSE and Qwen2.5-0.5B) and LID probing, then builds a steering method (ITLC). It never compares representations across independently trained models, seeds, modalities or scales, so its results bear on no version. The base-to-instruct language-vector transfer is a steering performance result for its own method, not a mapping between independent models.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is mostly right but incomplete. Authors confirm naturally emerging middle-layer cross-lingual alignment in Qwen2.5-0.5B and last-layer alignment in LaBSE. They find alignment is negatively correlated with LID information. The main contribution is ITLC, which mitigates language confusion (about +9% monolingual, +26.7% cross-lingual LPR) with minimal semantic loss.
record.recipe_differences: Measures cosine similarity between parallel-language inputs within a model and contrasts layers and two model types; it does not measure convergence between independently trained models as a function of scale.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured cosine similarity varies substantially by layer, especially in Qwen2.5-0.5B.

fits_no_version.finding: Cosine similarity of parallel sentences across languages peaks in the middle layer of Qwen2.5-0.5B (0.922 vs 0.591 first, 0.375 last). In LaBSE it is high in the middle and last layers (0.758, 0.754).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a multilingual model, representations of parallel sentences in different languages converge in specific layers. The layer depends on whether alignment is trained in (last layer) or emerges naturally (middle layers).

fits_no_version.finding: Language vectors extracted from base Qwen/Llama models steer the instruct variants about as well as native instruct vectors (Figure 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Language-specific directions are preserved between base and post-trained versions of the same model.

record.problems: The alignment comparison covers only LaBSE and one Qwen2.5 model size. The cosine figures reported in text are aggregate values across datasets, limiting assessment of dataset-specific variation. The measured construct is within-model cross-language alignment, not cross-model convergence.

untested.parts: No cross-model comparison and no scale sweep for alignment (only one 0.5B Qwen and LaBSE).
No cross-model mapping or stitching; base-to-instruct vector transfer is within one model lineage and is a steering result.
No feature or circuit comparison across models.
No cross-model convergence measured, so no metric dependence of it; only cosine similarity is used for within-model alignment.
No cross-model alignment, plateau, or causal-explanation analysis.

record.verdict_notes: The study's 'representation alignment' is a cross-lingual, within-model notion, not convergence between independently trained models. Relation is reclassified from tests/T3 to cites_only/T6; it does not even cite the Platonic paper. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No scale sweep or comparison of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
No vision-language comparison or image-caption pairs; the alignment tested is between languages within models.
No comparison across random seeds or shared-feature/subspace analysis.
No mapping between models, stitching, relative-representation transfer, or unpaired mapping.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
Uses cosine similarity and reports layer differences, but does not compare alternative similarity measures or separately report outcomes across input datasets.
No cross-model alignment, plateau analysis, or test of shared training data/objectives as an explanation.
